subject: Re: Datasphere RFP — Reservation runbook, GPU prioritization & sizing clarifications
messages:
From: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@datasphere.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataSphere Procurement <procurement@datasphere.com>, Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@datasphere.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Datasphere RFP — follow-up questions on dedicated reservations

Rachel — thanks again for the overview earlier this week. We reviewed the RFP and the initial sizing guidance you sent. A few clarifying questions came up from our procurement and infra teams before we move to a formal SOW: 

1) GPU family prioritization: you recommended H100 for peak latency-sensitive endpoints and A100-80GB for batch/embeddings. Can you outline the explicit tradeoffs you see in our workload (low-latency chat + nightly large-batch embedding refresh)? Specifically: tokens/sec per device, expected tail latency at 95/99, and recommended slot density for mixed workloads.

2) Reservation economics: our CFO wants to see a simple 3-scenario breakdown (conservative / base / aggressive) with committed monthly vCPU/GPU counts, burst lanes, and overage pricing. Can Redwood provide a template for that?

3) Failover & graceful degradation: in a region outage, what falls back first — quantized model variants, lower concurrency, or cross-region routing? We need the runbook snippet we can include in our procurement appendix.

Attached is our RFP excerpt (Datasphere_RFP_20271110.pdf) with section references (Sec 4.1–4.4) where we need short, explicit answers. Can you confirm a timeline for a consolidated reply and whether you can include a short runbook and workbook for our procurement?

Thanks — Oliver
Infrastructure & Cloud Procurement
DataSphere Inc.
[attachment: Datasphere_RFP_20271110.pdf (pdf)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@datasphere.com>
Cc: Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@datasphere.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Datasphere RFP — follow-up questions on dedicated reservations

Oliver — appreciate the clear asks. We can deliver the consolidated 3-scenario workbook + a short runbook snippet by next Tuesday (2027-11-16). High-level answers below and I will loop in our sizing leads for engineering specifics: 

1) GPU prioritization (summary):
- H100 (FP8/TF32): best for latency-sensitive LLM serve (chat, instruction) — higher tokens/sec for small batches and better tail performance for dynamic batching; recommended when 95th/99th percentile latency SLOs are <200ms for single-turn chat.
- A100-80GB (INT8/FP16): better price/throughput for large-batch embedding pipelines and high-context throughputs (long sequences). Use for nightly embedding refresh and quantized offline workloads.
- Suggested mix for hybrid: start with 60% H100 reserved slots for prod chat endpoints, 30% A100 for daily bulk jobs, 10% flexible burst/quantized pool. Exact split will depend on your concurrency profile.

2) Reservation economics: we will attach a 3-scenario sheet (conservative/base/aggressive) showing committed GPU months, estimated usable token throughput, and overage rates. The workbook will include a simple sensitivity column for a +/-20% usage variance.

3) Failover & graceful degradation: runbook summary will include: 1) automatic cross-region reroute (if allowed by contract), 2) model-variant fallback to quantized variant (e.g., bfloat/INT8) for non-critical endpoints, 3) per-route concurrency reduction and adaptive batching to preserve throughput, and 4) prioritized serving for P0 routes.

I will coordinate a short internal review with our SRE and pricing teams and send the attachments and a redlined runbook by 2027-11-16 EOD PT. If you have a preferred pricing horizon (12/24/36 months) call it out and we will model it.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Datasphere RFP — need sizing inputs and runbook snippet (internal)

Team — forwarding Datasphere's questions (see attached RFP). Need quick inputs so we can finalize the workbook and runbook for next Tuesday. Key asks below; please paste short bullets (one-liners) I can include verbatim.

Objectives: produce a 1-page technical appendix and a 3-scenario workbook (conservative/base/aggressive). Attachments: reserve_sizing_workbook.xlsx (draft) and redwood_reservation_runbook_v1.2.pdf (starter).

Questions:
A) GPU throughputs & tail latency guidance (numbers per device): for H100 and A100-80GB give tokens/sec for our target shapes — chat (max 512 tokens, median 64), embeddings (batch size 1024, sequence 256), and long-context inference (4096 tokens). Also provide 95/99ms latency estimates for chat with concurrency levels (1, 8, 32).
B) Suggested reservation cadence: given their projected monthly token units (they listed 4B tokens/month baseline, spiky to 6B), recommend committed GPU-months for each scenario and burst lane percentage.
C) Failure playbook snippet: concise stepwise fallback order for docs.

Please reply inline with short bullets by Monday 11/15 EOD so I have a day to weave into the workbook.

Thanks — r

[attachment: reserve_sizing_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@datasphere.com>
Cc: Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@datasphere.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 17:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Datasphere RFP — reservation runbook & 3-scenario workbook (attached)

Oliver / Aisha — attached are the consolidated materials: redwood_reservation_runbook_v1.2.pdf (runbook snippet + failover flow), and reserve_sizing_workbook.xlsx (3-scenario conservative/base/aggressive). Below are the concise answers called out in your RFP (Sec 4.1–4.4).

1) GPU family tradeoffs (consolidated):
- H100 (recommended for P0 chat): ~30–45 tokens/sec per device for short-turn chat (64 tokens median) at concurrency=8 with 95th latency ~110–160ms, 99th ~180–260ms depending on batching. At concurrency=1, tokens/sec is higher (~200–300) for single-turn optimized kernels.
- A100-80GB (recommended for embeddings & long-context): ~6–12k embeddings/sec (batch 1024, seq 256) depending on model size/quantization; long-context inference (4k tokens) shows ~4–10 tokens/sec depending on attention optimizations and sequence truncation. Tail latency is higher at 95/99 percentiles for long-context workloads.
- Mixed-pool guidance: start with H100 reserve pool equal to ~0.55 * (baseline chat capacity in GPU-months), A100 pool at ~0.35 for embedding throughput, and 0.10 flexible burst (either spot or autoscale) to handle peak batch windows.

2) 3-scenario reservation guidance (high level):
- Conservative: commit 18 GPU-months (12 H100 equiv, 5 A100-80GB, 1 flexible) — covers ~70% baseline, cheap overage allowed.
- Base: commit 30 GPU-months (18 H100, 10 A100, 2 flexible) — targets baseline + steady growth, burst lane 15% of capacity.
- Aggressive: commit 50 GPU-months (32 H100, 15 A100, 3 flexible) — minimizes overage and provides headroom for feature rollouts.
(Workbook contains token-to-GPU mapping, price ladders for 12/24/36 month terms, and overage tiers.)

3) Failover & graceful degradation (runbook excerpt):
Step 1 — Priority routing: route P0 routes to secondary region if primary region health degrades beyond threshold (see runbook thresholds).
Step 2 — Model variant fallback: switch to quantized variants (INT8/bfloat) for non-critical routes; flag human-in-loop for any degraded QA-sensitive outputs.
Step 3 — Concurrency taper: reduce per-route concurrency limits and enable aggressive batching for less-latency-critical requests.
Step 4 — Controlled feature gates: disable low-priority augmentations (e.g., tool-calls, multi-step pipelines) to conserve compute.
Step 5 — Customer communication & throttling: trigger SLA notice and incrementally broaden capacity or approve emergency burst lanes.

Attachments and links: 
- redwood_reservation_runbook_v1.2.pdf — includes a printable 2-page runbook appendix you can drop into procurement (attached).
- reserve_sizing_workbook.xlsx — three scenario tabs + sensitivity analysis (attached).
- HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/companies/DS-2027-081 (internal reference).

Next steps / asks:
- Please confirm which pricing horizon you want modeled (12 / 24 / 36 months) and whether cross-region failover is required in the SOW.
- If acceptable, we can convert the workbook into a short SOW appendix and provide draft contract language for capacity carve-outs.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you prefer a walkthrough.

Best regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0193
